findings.title: Crash when a Google Meet event has no destination calendar
findings.body: In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When the event has no destination calendar (null or empty array — e.g. an organizer without a connected destination calendar booking an event type whose location is Google Meet), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, failing the entire booking creation. The previous code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) safely fell back to Cal Video in exactly this case. Restore the optional chain: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for organization slug
findings.body: This PR changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting when the organization's `slug` column is written. Previously the slug was set only when team billing was disabled, and `requestedSlug` metadata was used when billing was enabled; now organizations created with billing disabled never get a `slug` (breaking their org subdomain/URL), while billing-enabled instances write `slug` directly, bypassing the requested-slug verification flow. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work and appears to have been pulled in accidentally.

findings.title: createEvent always targets the main host's calendar, breaking multi-host events on Office365
findings.body: createEvent takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and posts to `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. With collective events, EventManager now calls createEvent once per host credential, passing the full destinationCalendar array each time. For every host other than the organizer, `destinationCalendar[0]` is still the organizer's calendar, so the Graph API call uses this host's access token against a calendar ID belonging to a different user (or a non-Office365 calendar ID if the organizer uses another provider) — the request fails and that host never receives the event on their calendar. Like GoogleCalendarService now does, this should pick the destination calendar whose `credentialId` matches the credential being used (falling back to `/me/calendar/events`).

findings.title: createEvent uses the first destination calendar instead of the current host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent/createAttendees derive `calendarId` from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For collective bookings EventManager invokes createEvent once per host credential with the full array, so for any host other than the organizer the Lark API calls are made with that host's token against the organizer's calendar ID, which belongs to a different Lark account and will fail — the non-organizer host gets no calendar event. It should select the destination calendar matching the credential in use rather than always the first element.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for non-organizer hosts
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent (used by caldav/apple calendars) filters the account's calendars by `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For collective events, EventManager calls createEvent with each host's credential but the full destination array; for a non-organizer host, no calendar in their CalDAV account matches the organizer's externalId, so `responses` is empty, no error is thrown, and EventManager records a booking reference even though no event was ever written to that host's calendar. The destination calendar matching the current credential should be used.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when organizer/event type has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops, silently discarding the collected team calendars. For a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do, no calendar events are created for anyone (EventManager falls into its no-destination fallback path). Initialize to `[]` instead of `null` so the team hosts' calendars are always included.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback when externalCalendarId is missing is dead code, yielding undefined calendarId
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, which can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which let updates for older bookings (booking references without externalCalendarId) still target the destination calendar. Now those updates call `calendar.events.update` with `calendarId: undefined` and fail (e.g. rescheduling pre-existing bookings). The same dead fallback pattern exists in deleteEvent (line ~317), where it silently degrades to the "primary" calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: In the recurring + allRemainingBookings branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` takes only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. Now that collective bookings store one calendar reference per host, cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes only one host's calendar event per occurrence and leaves the other hosts' events orphaned on their calendars. Additionally, because this block now sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, it re-runs once per calendar reference of the cancelled booking, issuing duplicate delete attempts. Iterate all calendar references of each updated booking instead.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId, so meetings are not deleted on cancel
findings.body: In create(), referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results used `result.credentialId`, which createMeeting populates. With credentialId now persisted as null for video references, handleCancelBooking's check `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` fails, so the video meeting (Zoom, etc.) is never deleted when the booking is cancelled — an orphaned meeting link remains valid. Keep passing `result.credentialId` for video results.

findings.title: References created via updateLocation lose credentialId and externalCalendarId
findings.body: updateLocation's referencesToCreate now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent results never populate those fields, so every booking reference created through the edit-location flow is stored with null credentialId/externalCalendarId (previously they fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar`'s values). editLocation.handler persists these via `references: { create: ... }`, and later cancel/reschedule flows can no longer map these references to the correct credential and calendar — in multi-host bookings this means those calendar events can't be updated or deleted. Either have updateEvent return the reference's credentialId/externalCalendarId or keep the previous fallback.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId
findings.body: In createEvent, the insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"` but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the hangout link into the event description passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is undefined, which the new credentialId-based lookup allows), the patch is issued with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link never gets added to the event description. Use the same `|| "primary"` fallback as the insert.

findings.title: loadUsers no longer selects organization slug for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user (no eventTypeId) query that existed before this change. Any downstream logic relying on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic collective bookings (e.g. org-domain booker URLs) now receives undefined. If the removal wasn't deliberate, restore the select.

findings.title: loadUsers masks unexpected errors and leaks Prisma messages as 400s
findings.body: The new try/catch in loadUsers converts PrismaClientKnownRequestError into an HTTP 400 with the raw Prisma error message (exposing internal database error details to clients) and converts every other unexpected error into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", discarding the original error and making production failures undebuggable. Additionally, an empty dynamicUserList previously simply returned no users but now throws a 500. Consider letting errors propagate as before.

findings.title: No tests cover the new multi-host calendar fan-out
findings.body: The PR's central behavior change — createAllCalendarEvents creating one calendar event per destination calendar (including fetching other hosts' credentials from the DB) and updateAllCalendarEvents iterating multiple calendar references — has no unit or integration coverage; the only test change is an updated webhook payload expectation. Given this touches booking creation, reschedule, and cancellation for every calendar provider, at least one test exercising a collective booking with two hosts (verifying two references with correct credentialId/externalCalendarId, and that cancel/reschedule cleans up both) should be added.
